Yes, healing from an abusive relationship is absolutely possible, though the journey looks different for everyone. Many people find that rather than forgetting the trauma entirely, they're able to process it in ways that reduce its emotional hold over time. The memories may remain, but they can become less painful and intrusive as you heal.

Working with a trauma-informed therapist can be incredibly valuable—they can help you develop tools for managing difficult emotions, processing what happened, and rebuilding your sense of self and safety. Healing isn't linear, and being gentle with yourself during difficult moments matters. You've already shown remarkable strength by recognizing what you need and asking this question. If you're in the US, the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233) offers support and resources that might be helpful as you navigate this process.
